text:
Sensex and Nifty closed higher on 16 November, but mid and small caps closed lower - a split market.

• The Sensex rose 512.34 points (0.63%) to settle at 82,104.79, per Business Standard and Kotak Neo closing reports.
• The Nifty 50 settled at 25,291.10, up 146.80 points (0.58%), per the same reports.
• The Nifty Midcap 100 fell 0.51% and the Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 1.10%.
• FMCG was the top sectoral gainer on the NSE; reports cited profit booking in mid and small caps.

Our view: A day when the headline indices rise while the broader market falls is a reminder that an index level can hide very different experiences underneath. It may reflect a rotation towards large and defensive names, or simply profit booking after a strong run, and one session cannot tell us which. We would treat it as context for diversification, not as a signal.

Question for practitioners: when large caps and small caps diverge like this, do you review the allocation between them, or leave it to your long-term plan?
